title: O Lord, How Many Are My Foes
description: O Lord, How Many Are My Foes in Tonic Solfa to OLD HUNDREDTH, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 3, part 2, headed “A morning Psalm”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Long Metre (8.8.8.8). This page sets the words to OLD HUNDREDTH; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: O Lord, how man-y are my foes, In this weak state of flesh and blood! My peace they dail-y dis-com-pose, But my de-fence and hope is God.

lines: O Lord, how many are my foes,
In this weak state of flesh and blood!
But my defence and hope is God.
Tir'd with the burdens of the day,
To thee I rais'd an evening cry;
Thou heardst when I began to pray,
And thine almighty help was nigh.
I laid me down and slept secure;
Not death should make my heart afraid,
Tho' I should wake and rise no more.
But God sustain'd me all the night;
He rais'd my head to see the light,
And make his praise my morning song.

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to OLD HUNDREDTH by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
